timeline.event: Union Carbide introduced Dynel, the first modacrylic fiber.
Kaneka introduced Kanekalon modacrylic, which it describes as about 60% acrylonitrile and 40% vinyl chloride.
A full-size flash fire simulation measured acid deposition on skin traps under modacrylic blend coveralls.
California public health scientists reported modacrylic containing vinyl chloride and antimony, with fiberglass, in mattress cover fire barriers.

timeline.event: Poly(vinyl alcohol) was first made in Germany.
PVA was sold as Synthofil, a water-soluble fiber.
A formaldehyde treatment was developed to make PVA fibers insoluble, the basis of vinal or vinylon.
Kuraray industrialized PVA fiber, which it describes as the first synthetic fiber produced domestically in Japan.
North Korea built a large vinylon complex at Hamhung using coal and limestone feedstocks.
A study estimated how PVA from detergent pods moves through US wastewater treatment, with most leaving in sludge.

timeline.event: The American Viscose Corporation was manufacturing a vinyl chloride and vinyl acetate copolymer fiber, sold as vinyon.
Regulation (EU) No 1007/2011 set the EU fibre names, including chlorofibre for vinyl chloride based fibers.
A forensic study of commercial synthetic wigs recorded PVC fibers alongside modacrylic and polypropylene.
A report for the European Commission reviewed PVC additives and end-of-life issues in the context of a non-toxic environment.

timeline.event: Gore began replacing PTFE with expanded polyethylene (ePE) membranes in some Gore-Tex products from the Fall/Winter season.
Five national authorities submitted an EU restriction proposal in January covering about 10,000 PFAS, a class that includes fluoropolymers such as PTFE.
California AB 1817 began prohibiting intentionally added PFAS in most textile articles on 1 January, using a total organic fluorine threshold of 100 ppm.
ECHA published an updated PFAS restriction background document on 20 August after more than 5,600 consultation comments, adding derogations including some fluoropolymer uses.
Under AB 1817 the California total organic fluorine threshold for textile articles is scheduled to fall from 100 ppm to 50 ppm.

timeline.event: A needle-punched PTFE and PPS felt that becomes triboelectrically charged during processing was reported as a self-charging air filter.
Two studies addressed PPS's main weakness, oxidation of sulfur: a controlled pre-oxidation route (OPPS) and a polybenzoxazine coating for oxidation resistance.
A MnCeCoOx catalytic PPS filter destroyed about 78% of dioxins and furans and converted about 96% of nitric oxide at 200 C in a laboratory study.
A reduced graphene oxide coated PPS filter medium released about 75% of its dust cake at a blowback speed of 0.3 m/s, against about 62% for plain PPS, in a laboratory study.

timeline.event: Researchers reported a poly(ionic liquid) and OPBI composite membrane for high-temperature proton exchange fuel cells, part of the shift of PBI research toward membranes.
Studies described AB-PBI spinning from polyphosphoric acid solutions and reviewed electrospun PBI membranes for filtration and energy devices.
An ultralight PBI nanofiber foaming mat with a limiting oxygen index of 38% was reported as fluorine-free insulation for firefighting clothing.
